status_summary: Executive Order 14153 (signed 2025-01-20) directs Interior to review Alaska waterways for navigability with the State and prepare recordable disclaimers of interest. No blanket secretarial order shifting the burden of proof was found. BLM instead issued case-by-case decisions: on 2026-06-04 it announced four navigability decisions (Delta-Tangle, Fortymile tributaries, Kwethluk and Goodnews), the first for Alaska submerged lands since 2019, and on 2026-07-24 it found the Unuk River navigable at statehood and approved a disclaimer; on 2026-08-03 it issued two further decisions, approving disclaimers for the Arolik River system and (in part, with some reaches denied) the Eek River system.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14153 signed, directing Interior to review Alaska waterways for navigability with the State and to prepare recordable disclaimers of interest restoring ownership to the State as appropriate.
BLM announced four navigability decisions recognizing State of Alaska ownership of submerged lands under named river systems.
BLM approved a recordable disclaimer for the Unuk River after finding it navigable at statehood.

BLM approved in part and denied in part the State's application for the Eek River System, finding about 104 miles of the Eek River, about 47.5 miles of the Middle Fork Eek and a short Ugaklik River reach navigable at statehood and disclaiming federal interest in those submerged lands.

BLM approved the State's recordable disclaimer application for the Arolik River System, finding the Arolik River mainstem (about river miles 31.4 to 34.9), the East Fork Arolik River (river miles 0.0 to 11.4) and Arolik Lake navigable at statehood; lower reaches already conveyed and some administratively determined lands were excluded.

title: Recognize state ownership of Alaska navigable waters and submerged lands
